In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the axial ligand is not a major factor in determining the spectroscopic or redox properties of the primary donor of PSII.
the nature of axial ligands to PD1 is important in the case of PSII from Synechocystic PCC 680, but not in the case of the PSII from T. elongatus.
the axial ligand of PD1 does not affect P680 properties, at least in T. elongates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the properties of P680 are highly conserved among the different species of photosystem II.
the D1 histidine axial ligands to PD1 and PD2 are not important determinants of the properties of P680.
the redox and optical properties of P680 are highly dependent on the protein environment in which it resides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the D1 subunits from Synechocystisis PCC 6802 and T. elongatus are different with respect to their ability to tolerate mutations of the histidine ligand to the P680 chlorophyll.
